events.title: Wu Zetian proclaims herself emperor of China
events.description: Wu Zetian, long the power behind the Tang throne, took the title of emperor and founded her own Zhou dynasty. She remains the only woman to rule China in her own name, and expanded recruitment by examination.
events.html: Wu Zetian, long the power behind the Tang throne, took the title of emperor and founded her own Zhou dynasty. She remains the only woman to rule China in her own name, and expanded recruitment by examination.

events.title: Abd al-Rahman III becomes emir of Córdoba
events.description: Abd al-Rahman III became the eighth emir of Córdoba. He went on to reunite al-Andalus and in 929 proclaimed himself caliph, founding the Caliphate of Córdoba; his reign marked the height of Andalusi power.

events.title: Jadwiga is crowned king, not queen, of Poland
events.description: Jadwiga, youngest daughter of Louis I of Hungary, was crowned king of Poland, rather than queen, to highlight her sovereign status. Under the Union of Krewo she later married the Lithuanian grand duke Jogaila, beginning the dynastic union of Poland and Lithuania.

events.title: Jourdan's French army wins the Battle of Wattignies
events.description: After two days of combat at Wattignies, a French army under Jean-Baptiste Jourdan defeated a Coalition army directed by Prince Josias of Saxe-Coburg-Saalfeld. The victory allowed the French to raise the siege of Maubeuge.

events.title: Marie Antoinette is guillotined in Paris
events.description: After a two-day trial before the Revolutionary Tribunal, the former queen Marie Antoinette was executed on the Place de la Révolution. She was 37, and her husband Louis XVI had been executed nine months earlier.

events.title: The Battle of Leipzig begins
events.description: Austrian, Prussian, Russian and Swedish armies attacked Napoleon around Leipzig. With some 600,000 soldiers engaged over three days, the 'Battle of the Nations' was the largest in Europe before the First World War.
events.html: Austrian, Prussian, Russian and Swedish armies attacked Napoleon around Leipzig. With some 600,000 soldiers engaged over three days, the 'Battle of the Nations' was the largest in Europe before the First World War.

events.title: Margaret Sanger opens the first US birth control clinic
events.description: Margaret Sanger, her sister and a colleague opened a birth control clinic in Brownsville, Brooklyn. Police closed it nine days later, but Sanger's campaign led to the organisation that became Planned Parenthood.

events.title: Ten Nazi leaders are hanged at Nuremberg
events.description: Ten men sentenced by the International Military Tribunal, including Ribbentrop, Keitel and Streicher, were hanged in Nuremberg prison's gymnasium. Göring had taken poison the night before.
